text.value: 40-year operator · technologist · fractional CTO

text.label: Text: A CTO is a Chief Technology Officer — the pe…
text.value: A CTO is a Chief Technology Officer — the person who decides what software a company runs and makes all of it work together. Big companies pay one north of $200,000 a year. Fractional means part-time and shared, so a business your size can finally have one. I ran on my own from 1986 on.  The whole time I had the same recurring problem: I could never find people worth the effort — people who would stick around, take the training, and actually do the job right.

text.label: Text: A restaurant. A mortgage company. A roofing…
text.value: A restaurant. A mortgage company. A roofing company. A trucking company I ran for twenty years. And now this one — a technology company installing

text.label: Text: AI operating systems and processes.
text.value: AI employees, and the systems that run them.

text.label: Text: In every one of them I hit the same wall. An…
text.value: When I did find someone good, I could not keep them long enough for it to matter. They quit. They cut corners. They went off and did their own thing. So I gave up on it and did everything myself — the work, the books, the follow-up, the ads, and yes, I was the computer guy too.

text.label: Text: So I have sat in your exact chair, doing 90%…
text.value: So I have sat in your exact chair, longer than most of these consultants have been alive. I know what it feels like to be great at the work and still buried under every other job in the company. I have lived it four times. Steven James Consulting does not run that way — it has a team behind the work, and the systems that finally make a team worth having. That is the difference between then and now, and it is exactly what I install for you.

text.value: Software like your Website, Customer Relationship Management software, & email never did anything without your manual input.

text.label: Text: What changed
text.value: What changed

text.label: Heading: Every decade handed me a slightly better set…
text.value: Every decade handed me a slightly better set of software tools. None of them did the work. YET...

text.label: Text: Phone, fax, the first websites, email blasts…
text.value: Phone, fax, the first websites, email blasts, the customer-list software. Each one helped a little. But not one of them ever did the actual work. They sat there and waited for me to push the button. They were tools, and I was still the one holding them.

text.label: Text: That changed for good in 2024.
text.value: That changed for good in 2024.

text.label: Text: I could finally hire the employee I had been…
text.value: I could finally hire the employee I had been looking for my whole career — an AI employee. It takes the training. It does not quit. It does not go off and freelance. It does not call in sick or take days off. It answers every lead the second it comes in, follows up, books the appointment, and circles back on the cold ones. It does the job the same way every time, and I can see everything it does. That is what changed the math. The machines take the grinding, repetitive work that burned out every good person I ever hired — so a small team of people worth having can do what used to take a department. That is how this company runs, and it is what I install for you.

text.label: Heading: Almost everyone else selling AI is handing y…
text.value: Almost everyone else selling AI is handing you a chatbot.

text.label: Text: A little pop-up that answers one question an…
text.value: A little pop-up that answers one question and hands you back the work. That is not an employee.

text.label: Text: And here is what they will not tell you: the…
text.value: And here is what they will not tell you: the raw AI brains behind all of it — ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Grok, whichever one you have heard of — are something anyone can rent for a few dollars a month. We work with all of them, and a big part of the job is knowing which one to put on which job.

text.label: Text: But on its own, any of them is the smartest…
text.value: But on its own, any of them is the smartest worker you ever met who knows nothing about your business and forgets it all by morning — brilliant, and useless to you. The hard part, the part I have spent years on, is turning that raw brain into a real employee that knows your prices, your customers, and your way of doing things — and wiring it right into the software you already run.

text.label: Text: And every business runs on something differe…
text.value: And every business runs on something different. Whatever you picked up over the years to run yours, that is your setup, and getting the AI to actually talk to it — so the two run as one machine — is the part nobody else has cracked. We do it by hand, one business at a time.

text.label: Text: Why it matters
text.value: Why it matters

text.label: Heading: I have been the customer you are about to be…
text.value: I have been the customer you are about to be.

text.label: Text: I have hired agencies. I have been sold repo…
text.value: I have hired agencies. I have been sold reports full of impressions and clicks by people who had never made a payroll and could not tell me what a customer cost me. That is why this company works the way it does.

text.label: Text: An operator reads a profit and loss statemen…
text.value: An operator reads a profit and loss statement differently than a marketer reads a dashboard. When we talk about what a customer costs to acquire and what one is worth over the whole relationship, I am not quoting a framework — those are the numbers that decided whether I made money for forty years.

text.label: Text: The technology is the part I enjoy. Putting…
text.value: The technology is the part I enjoy. Putting AI on top of the software a business already runs is the most useful thing I have found in a long time, and it works because it does not ask a busy owner to change how they work.

props.text: Out of forty years and five businesses, this is the part I like best. Tying the systems together. Connecting the dots so a company runs as one machine instead of six disconnected ones.

Most owners find this side of the business boring — the tracking, the numbers, the KPIs, which is just the handful of figures that tell you whether the thing is actually working. I have never found it boring. If you cannot see those numbers, you do not know what is going on inside your own company. You are guessing.
So when an owner tells me he wants his systems connected and his numbers tracked, that is a good day for me. Those are my favorite people to work with.

And if it has never been your side of the business, it needs to become your side. That is the line between an operator and somebody who owns a job. An operator knows what a customer costs him, which system produced that customer, and what that customer was worth. Everybody else finds out how the year went when the accountant tells them.
I say that plainly because it is what I believe, and because it is the whole reason this company exists. A business that cannot see its own numbers cannot be improved by anything I sell it.
